title: Death blamed on alcohol abuse
article: A history of alcohol abuse -- not negligence -- was behind the death of a man taken into custody by police, a judge wrote in a report following a fatality inquiry.

In a report released Tuesday, Judge Catherine Skene said she had no recommendations following the death of Woodrow James Three Suns, noting there is no evidence to indicate there was any negligence by the Calgary Police Service, paramedics, nor Calgary Transit officers who had dealt with the 41-year-old man on the night he died.
Three Suns was taken into custody on June 2, 2007, after a Calgary Transit officer found him lying on the floor of a bus shelter at the Southland LRT station.
Because Three Suns had two outstanding warrants, transit officers took him to the Calgary Police Service's arrest processing unit.
Three Suns was put into the drunk tank, where officers checked on him every 10 minutes as required by the police service's policy, Skene wrote in her report.
During one of these checks, Three Suns was found to be unresponsive. Paramedics attempted to revive the man as an ambulance was called.
He was taken to the Peter Lougheed General Hospital, where he was pronounced dead at 4:37 a.m. on June 3.
